picks.why: True hat proportions with a modest brim curl and a thin pale edge. 2 has an oversized brim and heavy trim; 3 adds an invented star badge.
Bold, simple paisley and soft cloth match the real cards' restraint. 2's pattern is busier, and 3's open gap makes the cloth look thin and flat.
Deep sloped bowl with ridged sides reads as a gold pan. 2 is shallow and flat, so it reads as a frying pan.
Classic hurricane lantern with a clean bail, wire guard and balanced body. 2's bail is wobbly, and 1 lacks the guard and sits on a tilted plank.
Simple glaze bands and a sturdy jug shape with no extra decoration. 1 adds dots, and 3's filled band is more ornate with a slimmer neck.
Tight, compressed bale with neat straw and plain twine. 1 adds knotted tassels and shaggy straw, and 2 is messier.
Best barrel: tall bulge with stave tops rising above the top hoop and a lid that sits in place. 1 and 2 have lids that overhang like tabletops.
Rib definition and small spine nubs make it read as a real cactus rather than a smooth toy. 2's trunk is too fat, and 3 is plastic-smooth.
Most believable horse: solid body and head with legs of plausible length. 1 and 3 are long-legged and stilted.
Most restrained: thin gold trim, no curtains and a calmer palette, closest to the real cards' matte restraint. 1 and 2 are over-decorated with gold and curtains.
